name: Zurich
tagline: Banking grandeur, lakeside calm and Alpine air in one
bestMonths: May, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep
whenBlurb: June to September for lake days, alpine trails and the pre-Art-Basel art weekend, or December for ski access and Christmas markets; the shoulder months of spring are quiet and mild.

ourTake.lede: Zurich is easy to underrate as merely tidy and rich; give it a day or two and the lake, the swimmable river and a genuinely serious art scene reveal themselves. Prioritise the Kunsthaus and a slow afternoon on the water over ticking off the Bahnhofstrasse, and in summer swim where the locals do at the badis along the Limmat. It is compact, punctual and expensive, so plan fewer things and do them well.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a lakeside base, effortless trains and the Alps an hour away.
ourTake.skipIf: You are watching the budget or want warmth and a beach.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Baur au Lac
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: The city's grande dame since 1844, family-owned, lake-facing, and quietly the address that matters.

items.name: The Dolder Grand
items.description: A fairy-tale hillside resort above Zurich, a spa, an art collection and the whole lake laid out below.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental Savoy, Zurich
items.description: The city's oldest grand hotel, reborn, Mandarin Oriental precision on the Paradeplatz.

items.name: Widder Hotel
items.description: Nine medieval townhouses stitched into one, an art-and-design masterpiece in the heart of the Old Town.

items.name: La Réserve Eden au Lac Zurich
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A Philippe Starck-imagined 'yacht club' on the lake, playful, private and thoroughly of the moment.

items.name: Storchen Zürich
items.description: Six hundred years on the Limmat, a riverfront address woven into the fabric of the Old Town.

items.name: Park Hyatt Zurich
items.description: Cool, contemporary calm a step from Bahnhofstrasse, glass, art and space where the city is dense.

items.name: Marktgasse Hotel
items.description: A restored 15th-century house in the pedestrian Old Town, design-led, intimate, and full of history.

items.name: Alden Suite Hotel Splügenschloss Zürich
items.description: An all-suite mansion of 1895, quiet, discreet, and among the most private addresses in the city.

items.name: Kameha Grand Zürich
items.description: A Marcel Wanders design spectacle on the city's edge, bold, playful, and unlike anything in the Old Town.

items.name: 25hours Hotel Zurich West
items.description: A witty, design-forward base in the reinvented industrial west, excellent value by Zurich standards.

items.name: Grossmünster & the tower climb
items.description: Zurich's twin-towered Romanesque landmark, where Huldrych Zwingli launched the Swiss-German Reformation in the 1520s. Inside are choir windows by Augusto Giacometti and side windows by Sigmar Polke; climb the 187 steps of the Karlsturm for a close panorama over the Old Town roofs, the lake and the Alps beyond. A private guide can bring the Reformation history alive for older children and grandparents.

items.name: Fraumünster & the Chagall windows
items.description: A former abbey church on the elegant Münsterhof square, holding five stained-glass chancel windows designed by Marc Chagall in 1970 plus a rose window, among the most important works of modern religious art in Switzerland. Best in morning light when the colours flood the choir. Quiet, unhurried, and moving even for those with no interest in churches.

items.name: St. Peter's Church & Europe's largest clock face
credentials: Largest church clock face in Europe
items.description: Zurich's oldest parish church, whose tower carries the largest church clock face in Europe at roughly 8.7 metres across. A short, atmospheric stop between Lindenhof and Fraumünster; the surrounding lanes hide serious patisseries and boutiques for an easy stroll.

items.name: Lindenhof
items.description: A leafy hilltop terrace on the site of a Roman fort and later imperial palace, shaded by century-old linden trees, with one of the loveliest free views over the Limmat, the Old Town spires and Grossmünster. Locals play boules and chess here; a calm, camera-ready pause on a private walking tour, and a favourite spot for a golden-hour photograph.

items.name: Niederdorf (Dörfli) lanes
items.description: The pedestrianised heart of the Old Town, cobbled alleys winding up toward the Grossmünster, lined with boutiques, chocolatiers, cafés and long-standing patisseries. Best explored slowly on foot, ideally early evening; a private guide can thread you past the Cabaret Voltaire, Spiegelgasse and the quieter courtyards the crowds miss.

items.name: Bahnhofstrasse, the luxury mile
items.description: One of the most expensive shopping streets in the world, running from the main station to the lake. This is where Zurich's watches and jewellery live, the maisons, the grandes marques, and the great multi-brand houses, alongside international fashion. Stroll it end to end, then reward the family at Sprüngli on Paradeplatz. A concierge can arrange private after-hours appointments at the watch houses.

items.name: Beyer Chronometrie, Bahnhofstrasse
items.description: One of the world's oldest watch and jewellery houses, family-run since 1760, and a serious address for Patek Philippe, Rolex and the finest independents. The ground-floor salon is discreet and unhurried; ask for a private consultation. Below it sits the Beyer Clock and Watch Museum for the horology-minded.

items.name: Beyer Clock and Watch Museum
items.description: A jewel-box basement museum beneath the Beyer store on Bahnhofstrasse, tracing timekeeping from around 1400 BC to the present across some 270 objects, sundials, tower clocks, pocket watches and the prototype of the first quartz wristwatch. A short, rich stop that gives context before any watch purchase; a natural pairing for collectors.

items.name: Confiserie Sprüngli, Paradeplatz
items.description: The house that has stood at Paradeplatz since 1859, celebrated for its featherlight Luxemburgerli macarons and truffles. The upstairs café is a Zurich institution for a mid-morning coffee and cake; the boutique makes elegant, packable gifts to carry home. Reliable vegetarian sweets and a favourite treat for children and grandparents alike.

items.name: Lake Zurich cruise (ZSG)
items.description: The Lake Zurich Navigation Company runs daily scheduled cruises from the Bürkliplatz quay, from short 1.5-hour loops to longer runs past the villa-lined 'Gold Coast' to Rapperswil, aboard motor vessels and classic paddle steamers. Book a Dream Boat dinner or brunch cruise for a private-feeling occasion; the calm water and Alpine backdrop suit multi-generation groups.

items.name: Lakeside promenades, Bürkliplatz to Zürichhorn
items.description: The right-bank promenade runs from Bürkliplatz along the Utoquai to the parks at Zürichhorn, swans, plane trees, the Chinese Garden and, on clear days, the Alps mirrored in the water. A gentle, level walk perfect for grandparents and an evening stroll after dinner. Stop at the Pavillon Le Corbusier along the way.

items.name: Summer swimming at the Badis (Seebad Enge & Utoquai)
items.description: Zurich swims in its own lake and rivers in summer. Seebad Enge is a stylish lakeside lido with a sauna and a bar; the historic wooden Seebad Utoquai has welcomed swimmers off its docks for over 120 years. Clean, cold, and quintessentially local, a refreshing morning dip before the day's sightseeing.

items.name: Kunsthaus Zürich
items.description: Switzerland's largest art museum, expanded by a luminous David Chipperfield extension. The collection runs from Old Masters and a deep Giacometti holding to Munch, the Impressionists and Pipilotti Rist's immersive installations. Admission to the permanent collection is free on Wednesdays; a private docent can tailor a focused hour for the family.

items.name: Swiss National Museum (Landesmuseum)
items.description: Housed in a fairy-tale château beside the station, this is the most-visited museum of cultural history in Switzerland, a clear, beautifully staged journey through Swiss history, craft and identity, watches and design included. Excellent for context on your first day, and engaging for older children.

items.name: Museum Rietberg
items.description: Switzerland's only major museum of non-European art, set in three historic villas in the emerald Rieterpark above the lake. Strong Indian, Chinese, Japanese, African and Himalayan collections, of particular resonance for Indian visitors, shown with real care. Combine with a stroll through the park for one of the city's calmest cultural afternoons.

items.name: FIFA Museum
items.description: Three floors of football history opposite Bahnhof Enge, with the original World Cup trophy on display, over 1,000 pieces of memorabilia and hands-on digital stations. A genuine highlight for football-mad teenagers and a fine rainy-day option; interactive enough to hold a mixed-age group.

items.name: Uetliberg, Zurich's home mountain
items.description: The 871-metre mountain rising over the city, reached in about 20 minutes on the S10 train from the main station. From the lookout tower the whole of Zurich, the lake and, on clear days, the Alps unfold below. Gentle ridge walks, a summit restaurant and easy access make it a relaxed half-day with sweeping photographs.

items.name: Zurich Zoo & Masoala Rainforest
items.description: One of Europe's most respected zoos, home to over 300 species, the vast Kaeng Krachan elephant park and the Lewa Savanna. Its showpiece is the Masoala Rainforest hall, a walk-through slice of Madagascar with free-flying birds, lemurs and dense green heat. A sure hit for children; reach it by tram or the funicular up the Zürichberg.

items.name: Lindt Home of Chocolate, Kilchberg
credentials: World's largest chocolate fountain (Guinness World Record)
items.description: The Lindt & Sprüngli chocolate experience just outside the city, built around the world's tallest chocolate fountain at over nine metres, an interactive museum and a generous free tasting zone. Book a chocolate-making workshop for the family, and stock the largest Lindt shop in the world with gifts to carry home. Reachable by a short train or lake boat.

items.name: Zürich West, the Viadukt
items.description: A restored 19th-century railway viaduct whose brick arches now hold design boutiques, a covered market hall and cafés, the beating heart of the city's reinvented industrial west. Graze the market hall for lunch, browse Swiss makers, and feel a grittier, more creative Zurich than Bahnhofstrasse.

items.name: Frau Gerolds Garten & Prime Tower
items.description: An urban garden of shipping-container shops, a summer beer garden and street food beneath the Prime Tower, at 126 metres one of Switzerland's tallest buildings. A relaxed, in-the-know spot for a sundowner; ride up to the Clouds restaurant and bar in the tower for a skyline view over the district.

items.name: Zurich Opera House (Opernhaus)
items.description: A grand 19th-century opera house on the lakefront, one of Europe's most respected houses for opera and ballet. Book a box for an evening in your finest; the neo-Baroque interior and the square outside make it an occasion in itself. A concierge can secure premium seats and pre-theatre dining nearby.

items.name: Tonhalle Zürich
items.description: The 1895 concert hall of the Tonhalle Orchester Zürich, its acoustics ranked among the finest in Europe and its gilded interior beautifully restored. An evening of world-class symphonic music in an intimate, ornate room, a refined alternative to a night at the opera.

items.name: Old Botanical Garden (Alter Botanischer Garten)
items.description: A small, romantic city-centre garden laid out on a former bastion, with a historic domed palm house and quiet terraced lawns. A green pause a few minutes from the shopping, pleasant for grandparents and children needing a breather between museums.

items.name: Pavillon Le Corbusier
items.description: The last building Le Corbusier designed, his only work in steel and glass, a jewel of primary-coloured panels set in the lakeside park at Zürichhorn. Open roughly May to November; a short, distinctive stop for design lovers, easily folded into a lake promenade walk.

items.name: Cabaret Voltaire
items.description: The tiny room at Spiegelgasse 1 where the Dada movement was born in 1916, now a café-bar and cultural space. A niche but genuine piece of art history tucked into the Old Town lanes, worth a coffee and a glance for the culturally curious.

items.name: James Joyce's grave, Fluntern Cemetery
items.description: In the leafy Fluntern cemetery on the Zürichberg lies James Joyce, who spent his final years in Zurich, marked by a seated bronze statue of the writer, book in hand. A quiet literary pilgrimage that pairs naturally with a visit to the nearby zoo.

items.name: Polybahn funicular & ETH terrace
items.description: A short, historic funicular climbs from Central up to the ETH university terrace, where one of the city's best free viewpoints looks back over the Old Town, the Limmat and the lake. A quick, characterful ride and a fine photo stop, especially at dusk.

items.name: Rhine Falls at Schaffhausen (day trip)
credentials: Largest waterfall in Europe by volume
items.description: The largest waterfall in Europe by volume, thundering over a 23-metre drop amid vineyards about 45 minutes north of the city. Boat trips carry you to the rock in the middle of the falls, and Schloss Laufen looks down from above. A dramatic, easy day out; pair it with medieval Stein am Rhein nearby.

items.name: Stein am Rhein (day trip)
items.description: A perfectly preserved medieval town on the Rhine, its main square ringed by half-timbered houses covered in vivid painted frescoes and oriel windows. Small, walkable and postcard-pretty, an easy, gentle addition to a Rhine Falls day, well suited to a relaxed pace with grandparents.

items.name: Lucerne & the Chapel Bridge (day trip)
credentials: Kapellbrücke, Europe's oldest surviving covered wooden bridge
items.description: Central Switzerland's loveliest lake town, under an hour by direct train, built around the Kapellbrücke, Europe's oldest covered wooden bridge, dating to the 14th century. Wander the old town, the frescoed bridge and the lakefront; an effortless, scenic day, and the gateway to Pilatus and Rigi.

items.name: Mount Pilatus 'Golden Round Trip' (day trip)
items.description: The classic mountain day from Zurich via Lucerne, combining a lake steamer, the world's steepest cogwheel railway, a rotating cable car and a panoramic gondola to a summit above the clouds. A thrilling, effortless Alpine experience for the whole family; a private driver-guide can smooth the connections.

items.name: Mount Rigi, 'Queen of the Mountains' (day trip)
items.description: A broad, gentle summit above Lake Lucerne reached by Europe's oldest mountain railway, with meadow walks, thermal baths at Rigi Kaltbad and 360-degree Alpine views. Softer and less vertiginous than Pilatus, ideal for a mixed-age group wanting mountains without the drama. Best on a clear day.

items.name: Mount Titlis & Engelberg (day trip)
credentials: World's first rotating cable car (Titlis Rotair)
items.description: Year-round glacier and snow at 3,000-plus metres, reached from the monastery village of Engelberg via the world's first rotating cable car, plus a cliff walk suspension bridge and a glacier cave. The most reliable place near Zurich to put the family in real Alpine snow whatever the season.

items.name: Zürichberg forest walk
items.description: The wooded ridge above the city, laced with easy trails, clearings and a wildlife park, reached by tram or funicular. A green, restorative morning away from the crowds, with occasional views down to the lake, pleasant for a slow family walk before a zoo or cemetery visit nearby.

items.name: Freitag Tower, Zürich West
items.description: A stack of 17 rusted shipping containers forming the flagship of Zurich's cult Freitag brand, whose bags are cut from used truck tarpaulins, climb to the top for a view over the western district. A quirky design pilgrimage and a distinctly Swiss, one-of-a-kind gift to take home.

items.name: Rapperswil, the 'town of roses' (lake day trip)
items.description: The pretty medieval town at the far end of Lake Zurich, crowned by a hilltop castle, famous for its rose gardens and a long wooden pilgrim's bridge across the water. Reach it languidly by boat and return by train, a gentle, scenic half-day at an unhurried pace.

items.name: Chinagarten (Chinese Garden)
items.description: A serene walled Chinese garden by the lake, a gift from Zurich's twin city Kunming, with pavilions, a koi pond and ornate gates. A small, tranquil detour on the lakeside promenade, a quiet, contemplative pause that reads well with grandparents.

items.name: Grossmünster to Fraumünster river walk
items.description: The short, storybook walk that ties the Old Town together, crossing the Limmat between the two great churches, past the guild houses, the Rathaus and the Wühre riverfront. Best at golden hour when the water glows; the ideal orientation stroll for a first evening in the city.

items.name: The Restaurant
items.description: Heiko Nieder's classical-modern cooking, laced with exotic accents, the city's benchmark table, high above the lake.

items.name: Widder Restaurant
items.description: Stefan Heilemann bridges classic haute cuisine and Thai-inflected modernity, the Old Town's two-star jewel.

items.name: The Counter
items.description: Mitja Birlo's surprise menu at a U-shaped counter beside the open kitchen, two stars from a standing start, inside the station.

items.name: IGNIV Zürich by Andreas Caminada
items.description: Caminada's fine-dining-meets-sharing concept, generous, playful and technically exact.

items.name: Orsini
items.description: Dario Moresco's creative modern Italian, guided by Milan's two-star Antonio Guida, bold contrasts, beautifully balanced.

items.name: La Rôtisserie
items.description: Refined cooking in a 14th-century riverside room, the Limmat gliding past the window.

items.name: Mesa
items.description: Sebastian Rösch's precise, light cooking, classical foundations with a bright, modern hand.

items.name: Kle
items.description: Entirely vegan fine dining with Moroccan and Mexican accents, creative, seasonal and quietly radical.

items.name: Neue Taverne
items.description: Nenad Mlinarevic's purely vegetarian, market-driven cooking in the heart of the Old Town.

items.name: Shin
items.description: An intimate Japanese counter, omakase sushi for a handful of guests, prepared before you.

items.name: Ornellaia
items.description: Modern Italian with a namesake cellar, Bolgheri's great wines beside a considered kitchen.

items.name: La Muña
items.description: Nikkei cooking, Peru meets Japan, on a lively rooftop above the shopping street.

items.name: Kronenhalle
credentials: A globally renowned historic dining room
items.description: A Zurich institution since 1924, Swiss and Viennese classics served beneath Chagall, Picasso and Miró.

items.name: Marguita
items.description: The Baur au Lac's signature room, Mediterranean-leaning cooking with the hotel's long-held polish.

items.name: Baur's
credentials: Swiss Bar Awards, Best Hotel Bar (2025)
items.description: A deluxe brasserie of the classics, Zürcher Geschnetzeltes and sole done immaculately.

items.name: Sushi Shin
items.description: Masami Okamoto's exclusive omakase for a few guests a night, pure, exacting Japanese craft.

items.name: Rosi
items.description: Markus Stöckle's self-styled 'neo-Bavarian' room, vivid, warm and unexpectedly refined.

items.name: EquiTable
items.description: Julian Marti's small, values-led kitchen, food, wine and service in quiet, sustainable harmony.

items.name: Gaijin Izakaya
items.description: A modern izakaya of real quality, Japanese small plates and charcoal, at an honest price.

items.name: Gül
items.description: Contemporary Turkish over wood and charcoal, a bright surprise menu that punches far above its price.

items.name: Freilager La Trattoria
items.description: Antonio Colaianni's lively trattoria, vitello tonnato and tiramisù finished at your table.

items.name: AuGust
items.description: Honest Swiss cooking, sausage, rösti and beer done properly, without a shred of ceremony.

items.name: Kronenhalle Bar
credentials: A genuine Zurich institution; the bar of the historic Kronenhalle (1924), with original art on the walls and Diego Giacometti lighting
items.description: Cocktails mixed beneath real Miró, Klee and Chagall, under lamps Diego Giacometti made for the room, a Zurich rite since the 1960s.

items.name: Widder Bar
credentials: Widder Hotel bar; long regarded among the best bars in Europe, celebrated for its 1,000+ spirits and whisky selection
items.description: Over a thousand spirits and a legendary whisky wall, with live jazz some nights, one of Europe's most respected hotel bars.

items.name: Old Crow
credentials: One of Zurich's most acclaimed cocktail bars, renowned for a 1,600+ bottle back-bar of rare spirits
items.description: A spirits pilgrimage, 1,600-odd bottles, rare whiskies and forgotten liqueurs, mixed with quiet precision.

items.name: Clouds
credentials: The city's highest bar, atop the 126m Prime Tower; own award-winning CLOUDS gin
items.description: Zurich's highest bar, the 35th floor, the Limmat valley and the Alps through the glass, best caught at sunset.

items.name: Jules Verne Panorama Bar
credentials: A landmark panorama bar in the historic Urania tower, above Brasserie Lipp
items.description: A round bar in the old Urania observatory tower, the Old Town, the lake and the Alps wrapped around you.

plan.heading: 3 days in Zurich, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: The old town, at a walk

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Coffee at Confiserie Sprüngli on Paradeplatz, then a slow loop through the Niederdorf lanes to the Grossmünster and across to the Fraumünster for the Chagall windows.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Walk the Bahnhofstrasse for the watch houses, Beyer, Türler, then along the lake promenade to Bürkliplatz.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Kronenhalle, the old dining room hung with Picasso and Miró, over a Zürcher Geschnetzeltes and a bottle of Bordeaux.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Kunsthaus for the Giacometti and Munch rooms, unhurried, before the tour groups arrive.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The boat from Bürkliplatz down the Zürichsee to Rapperswil, lunch on the water, and back.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at IGNIV by Andreas Caminada in the Marktgasse Hotel, the sharing table, the Grand Restaurant of the Year.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: The Uetliberg and the quiet side

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Train up the Uetliberg for the ridge walk and the whole city laid out below the Alps.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Rietberg Museum in Rieterpark for non-European art, then tea in the park's villa.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A last dinner at Rico's in Küsnacht along the lake, or the tavern room at Widder Hotel if you'd rather stay in town.

items.name: Altstadt (Old Town)
items.description: The medieval core around the Limmat with the churches and best hotels; suits those wanting to walk to everything.

items.name: Kreis 5 (Zürich West)
items.description: The reinvented industrial district of galleries, design and nightlife under the viaduct arches; suits a younger, design-minded stay.

items.name: Seefeld
items.description: The refined lakeside quarter of good restaurants and swimming spots; suits those who want calm near the water.

events.name: Sechseläuten
events.note: Zurich's guild spring festival, culminating in the burning of the Böögg snowman to predict the summer.

events.name: Street Parade
events.note: The world's largest techno street party, drawing hundreds of thousands along the lakefront.

events.name: Zurich Film Festival
events.note: The city's international film festival brings premieres and stars to venues across the centre.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Base yourself around the Baur au Lac or the lower Bahnhofstrasse for lake and old-town access; the Swiss run on punctuality, so a car arriving to the minute is expected, not exceptional.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: You land at Zurich Airport (ZRH), a fast, orderly hub, where a chauffeured car meets you plane-side or at arrivals for the 20-minute run into the city.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: The old town and lakefront are best walked; a private car and driver covers anything further, and the trams are immaculate if you ever wish to use them.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Coverage is total; an eSIM (Swisscom or Salt) activates on landing and hotel wifi is fast throughout.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Swiss francs (CHF); cards are accepted everywhere and contactless is standard, so cash is rarely needed and tipping is modest, rounding up or 5–10 percent for exceptional service.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: June to September is warm and clear, ideal for the lake and day-trips into the Alps; January and February are cold and grey with short days, better skipped unless you want the Christmas markets in December.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi on SWISS and Air India, about 8h45; from Mumbai and Bengaluru it is usually one stop via Zurich, Frankfurt, Munich or a Gulf hub. SWISS business is the natural choice; if connecting, the SWISS lounge at Zurich airport is a short, calm transfer with fast onward rail into the city.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required beyond routine; Switzerland is among the safest countries in the world, with negligible street crime. Tap water is excellent everywhere, so no bottled water needed.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain travel very easily. Zurich has Hiltl, the world's oldest vegetarian restaurant, plus South Indian veg at Saravanaa Bhavan; several Indian kitchens such as Delhi House will prepare Jain dishes on request.
